sentences.text:
Heard Mr. A.K. Chaturvedy, learned counsel for the  appellant and learned Spl. P.P.
This application has been preferred on behalf of appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Section 376(AB) IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years along with a fine of Rs. 25,000/- for the offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
It has been alleged that the appellant had taken the daughter of the informant near a Mahua tree and had committed rape upon her as a result of which blood has come out from her private parts.
Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the medical report does not support the factum of rape and, in fact, no injury was found on the person of the victim.
It has further been submitted that the appellant himself was aged 14 years at the time of the incident.
Learned counsel adds that the FSL report also does not indicate about the involvement of the appellant in committing rape upon the victim.
It has been submitted that the appellant is in custody for almost 4 years.

It has further been submitted that the appellant has been falsely implicated on account of a previous enmity which can be borne out from the cross-examinations of P.W.4, P.W.5,
P.W.6 and P.W.7.

sentences.text: 1 Learned Spl. P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

It appears that though the evidence of the witnesses suggests that the victim was subjected to penetrative assault, but neither the medical report nor the FSL report is corroborative of the said fact and the evidence of the some of the witnesses does indicate a semblance of enmity which might be a cause for implicating the appellant.

On consideration of the aforesaid facts, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail. Accordingly,
during pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-I-cum- Special Judge Children Court, Latehar in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 12/2021.
